identity.title: JWST detection of extremely excited outflowing CO and H<SUB>2</SUB>O in VV 114 E SW: A possible rapidly accreting IMBH

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have also retrieved archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of CO ($J=3-2$) and its associated 345 GHz continuum from program 2013.1.00740.S (PI: T. Saito).

evidence.quote: We adopt a distance to VV 114 of 88 Mpc.
we use the redshift of the bulk of the gas in SW-s2, $z=0.02013$, derived from the CO ($3-2$) line fit.

distance_source.value: adopted, not stated where from (z from CO(3-2) fit)

evidence.quote: We adopt a distance to VV 114 of 88 Mpc.
we use the redshift of the bulk of the gas in SW-s2, $z=0.02013$, derived from the CO ($3-2$) line fit.

question.value: What is the nature of the extremely excited, outflowing CO and H2O absorption bands detected with JWST in the SW-s2 clump of VV 114 E, and does it indicate an accreting IMBH?

evidence.quote: Here we report and analyze the detection of extremely excited CO and H$_2$O, observed in absorption, in the local merger VV 114
from program 2013.1.00740.S (PI: T. Saito)
observations of CO ($J=3-2$) and its associated 345 GHz continuum
as seen with the ALMA angular resolution of $0.14''\approx60$ pc
We have also retrieved archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations

other_facilities.name: JWST (NIRSpec IFU, MIRI MRS/imaging, NIRCam), DD-ERS 1328

provided.value: Main data: CO v=1-0 and H2O nu2 absorption bands, mid-IR images and spectra

evidence.quote: We have used the MIRI (imaging and MRS), NIRCam, and NIRSpec IFU data on VV 114 from the Director’s Discretionary Early Release Science (DD-ERS) Program #1328

what.value: HITRAN2020 spectroscopic parameters for CO and H2O

evidence.quote: We take all spectroscopic parameters for CO and H$_2$O from the HITRAN2020 database

what.value: Collisional rates for CO-H2 and H2O-H2

evidence.quote: using the rates by (cite: yan10) for collisional excitation of CO with H$_2$, and those by (cite: dan11) for H$_2$O with H$_2$

continuum_subtraction.value: 345 GHz continuum extracted from line-free channels; CO(3-2) shown as continuum-subtracted moment 0

evidence.quote: The images of the continuum-subtracted CO ($3-2$) emission (moment 0) and 345 GHz continuum (extracted from line-free channels) are shown in Fig. 1a-b

what.value: ALMA CO(3-2) and continuum images follow earlier publication of the data

evidence.quote: 345 GHz continuum (extracted from line-free channels) are shown in Fig. 1a-b (cite: sai15).
All details of the reduction procedure are given in (cite: gber23) and (cite: per23).
We use the code described in (cite: gon98), which assumes spherical symmetry.

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration, CASA version, imaging parameters (robust, beam, rms) for CO(3-2) and continuum
Aperture centre coordinates of the extraction
Line-free channels used for the 345 GHz continuum
Flux conversion details for CO(3-2) mass beyond alpha_CO value
Source code of the radiative transfer model

analysis_steps.goal: Fit CO(3-2) profile and set upper limit for hot component

method.value: 3-component Gaussian fit to CO(3-2) profile with one component fixed at -160 km/s, from aperture r=0.162''

evidence.quote: A 3-components Gaussian fit to the CO ($3-2$) profile, fixing the central velocity of one component at $-160$ km s$^{-1}$
using $\alpha_{\mathrm{CO3-2}}\approx0.8\,M_{\odot}/(\mathrm{K\,km\,s^{-1}\,pc^2})$
We have used the Paris-Durham shock code (cite: god19) to generate both $C-$type and $J-$type shock models
The observations were processed using the JWST Calibration pipeline (version 11.16.20).
The central velocity component has a CO ($3-2$) flux of $(17.4\pm0.1)$  Jy km s$^{-1}$

results_numeric.quantity: Upper limit CO(3-2) flux of hot component

evidence.quote: upper limit for the flux of the $H_C$ in CO ($3-2$) of $<0.35$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
$M_{\mathrm{gas}}(\mathrm{SW-s2})\sim3\times10^7\,M_{\odot}$

$$M_{\mathrm{BH}}=(4.5\pm2.4)\times10^4
\exp\{\tau_{\mathrm{6\mu m}}^{\mathrm{ext}}-2.5\}\,M_{\odot},

findings_qualitative.value: CO and H2O bands are radiatively excited by a ~550 K mid-IR blackbody and outflow at ~180 km/s

evidence.quote: the rotational levels of the ground vibrational state of CO and H$_2$O are radiatively excited by the mid-IR continuum

claims.experiment: Modelled JWST CO and H2O bands, compared with ALMA CO(3-2)
claims.result: L_IR ~1e10 Lsun in a sub-pc source; M_BH ~4.5e4 Msun, super-Eddington
claims.finding: SW-s2 is a possible rapidly accreting IMBH

evidence.quote: this result favors an IMBH in SW-s2

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Collisional excitation by shocks rejected as it fails to reproduce the required column densities

evidence.quote: but failed to reproduce the required column densities of warm molecular gas.

limitations_admitted.value: Source size not directly measured; IR surface density relies on assumed connected structure

evidence.quote: is not based on direct measurements of the source size.

referee_caveats_inferred: Hot component not detected in ALMA; ALMA role is minor and cannot test the model
BH mass depends on assumed lifetime and extinction

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data retrieved from the archive; JWST data from MAST

evidence.quote: We have also retrieved archival Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations

reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA role minor with few details; analysis relies on an unreleased code.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results come from JWST modelling with an unreleased code.

companion_papers.why: Similar JWST CO band analysis in NGC 3256
